transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because work has been getting kind of hard to manage. I do bookkeeping, and I keep finding myself going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I know I’ve already checked them, but I still feel like I need to do it one more time.

Sometimes I stay after everyone else has left just to recheck things. It sounds a little excessive, I know… but if I don’t, I get this awful feeling that something bad might happen and it would be my fault. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel anxious or uncomfortable in public places, like crowds, public transportation, or open spaces, because you worry it might be hard to escape or get help if something went wrong?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, crowds or buses aren’t my favorite or anything, but I don’t usually worry about not being able to escape or get help. That hasn’t really been the main problem for me, if that’s okay to say.
Have you ever had thoughts that seem intrusive or unwanted that bother you, like ideas or images popping into your head that you can’t seem to get rid of, even if you try not to think about them?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but even after I know the numbers match, this thought just jumps in like, what if I missed one hidden mistake? Like in payroll or taxes, and then someone’s check doesn’t go through, or the firm gets in trouble.

I try to tell myself I already looked and it’s fine, but it kind of comes right back. It’s like I can’t trust what I’m seeing, even when I know I checked it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Do you feel like you have to perform certain actions, like checking or rechecking things, in a specific way or a certain number of times to reduce your anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I think I do. Mostly with the spreadsheets and calculations. I’ll check them, and then I know I’ve checked them, but I still feel like I have to go back over them again… like just one more time.

It’s not always a specific number exactly, but it has to feel right, I guess. And if I don’t do it, I get really anxious, like something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Sometimes I end up staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves because I can’t stop rechecking. I know that probably sounds like too much.
Outside of work, do you find these kinds of thoughts or the need to check things interfering with your daily life, like at home or with family and friends?

A little, yeah… I mean, I try not to let it, but it has started spilling over. I’ve missed choir rehearsals and some youth-center things because I just can’t get out of the office on time. I keep thinking I’m almost done, and then I check something again.

And… I did miss a filing deadline once, which was really embarrassing. I got called into a formal meeting at work about it. I know that sounds bad. I’m not trying to make excuses, I just… I get stuck there, and then everything else gets pushed aside.
Do these thoughts or the need to keep checking things ever cause you a lot of distress, even when you’re not at work?

Yeah… I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just work stuff, but it does upset me a lot. Even when I’m not at work, I’ll think about the spreadsheets or calculations and whether I should’ve checked them again.

That’s kind of why I’m here, I guess. I can’t seem to stop going back over the same things again and again. Sometimes I stay for hours after everyone else leaves, even though I already checked them. It feels like if I don’t do it one more time, something bad might happen and it would be my fault. Is that… does that make sense?
Have you noticed these kinds of thoughts or the need to check things in areas of your life outside of work, like at home or with personal tasks?

I’m not sure… not really in the same way, I don’t think. It’s mostly work that I notice it with.

At home I might double-check something here or there, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. I haven’t really noticed it taking over personal tasks the way it does with the spreadsheets. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
